ai.title: Hide referral banner for unauthenticated users
ai.summary: Referral banner in `web/src/components/ui/banner.tsx` now checks `session?.user` via `useSession` and returns `null` if absent. Prevents unauthenticated users from seeing a banner that requires login to claim credits. Scope limited to web UI component. Condition updated to `if (!isVisible || !session?.user) return null`.

eli5.text: When you visit the site without being signed in, you will no longer see the banner offering referral credits at the top of the page; it now only appears once you are logged in. The page simply checks whether you have an active account before deciding whether to display that banner, so the message disappears entirely if you are not signed in. Since this only changes what shows on the website right now, nothing else about the site looks different.

ai.title: Navbar right alignment
ai.summary: Added `ml-auto` to the navbar `nav` element in `web/src/components/navbar/navbar.tsx`. This pushes the links to the right side of the container, preventing distraction from the logo.

eli5.text: When you open the web app, the navigation links (like Docs) now sit on the right side of the top bar instead of starting right after the logo on the left. The bar uses extra space on the left so the links are pushed to the right, keeping your focus on the main logo. You would notice this just by looking at the top of the page, the links have shifted to the right.

ai.title: New home page with concise title, video
ai.summary: Home page layout simplified to a concise headline and an inline autoplaying video, replacing the previous multi-section structure with a modal-triggered demo and terminal install snippet. The change is scoped to the web package, specifically `web/src/app/page.tsx` and `web/src/lib/constant.ts`. A new binary asset `web/public/codebuff-intro1.mp4` is added to support the inline video, while the site description in constants is updated to match the new headline.

eli5.text: When you open the site today, you'll see a short headline that says 'Code faster with AI' instead of the old multi-section layout, along with an autoplaying, silent video demonstration right on the page. Previously, you had to click a button to open a demo in a pop-up window and read a terminal install snippet; now that demo plays directly inline as a video. The site's description text that search engines and link previews pick up has been updated to match the new headline. The change is live and visible to anyone visiting the home page.

ai.title: Add webm fallback to intro video
ai.summary: Home page intro video adds `/codebuff-intro1.webm` as `<source>` fallback alongside existing MP4. New `disableRemotePlayback` and `preload="auto"` attributes added to `<video>` element. Scope: `web/src/app/page.tsx`, `web/public/codebuff-intro1.webm`.

eli5.text: You can now watch the intro video on the home page even if your browser prefers the webm format over mp4, since the site will automatically pick whichever version works best for your device. Behind the scenes, the video element now includes a remote-playback lock and preloads the clip ahead of time, so it starts up faster and won't accidentally cast to a nearby TV or streaming stick without your permission. The new video file and updated page are live today, so the next time you load the home page you'll get a smoother, more compatible playback experience without changing any settings.

ai.title: Add tab completion for file paths and token names in CLI
ai.summary: Tab completion added to CLI readline interface using `completer` callback. Matches file paths from `fileContext.fileTree` and token names from `fileTokenScores`. Client now exposes `fileContext` publicly, updated during `initFileVersions` and file change actions. Scope limited to `npm-app/src/cli.ts` and `npm-app/src/client.ts`.

eli5.text: When you open the typing box in the assistant's text chat, you can now press Tab to auto-fill file names from your project and the names of variables (tokens) the assistant uses. The assistant now keeps the list of your files and their associated variables available so it can offer those names as suggestions, and this list is kept up to date when files change. If you look at a project, start typing a file or variable name and hit Tab, you will see matching suggestions appear, making it faster to reference the right files and variables without typing them fully.
